blocks.prompt: 1 (i) Find the three cube roots of \(8\).
blocks.explanation: Dekhiye, yeh cube root wala sawal hai. Humein number 8 diya gaya hai aur woh tamam numbers \(x\) find karne hain jin ka cube (teesri power) 8 ho. Bohat se students sirf ek real jawab likh kar ruk jaate hain, lekin yaad rakhiye: har non-zero number ke teen cube roots hote hain, ek real aur do complex. Teeno tak pohanchne ka pakka tareeqa yeh hai: pehle \(x^{3}=8\) ko "kuch = 0" ki shakal mein likhenge, phir difference of cubes ke formula se factorize karenge. Linear factor (jis mein \(x\) ki power 1 ho) se real root milega aur quadratic factor se do complex roots. Aakhir mein complex roots ko \(\omega\) ki madad se saaf shakal mein likh denge.
steps:
Step 1: Sawal ko equation mein badlein
\[x^{3}=8\]
\[x^{3}-8=0\]
\[x^{3}-2^{3}=0\]
Kyun: 8 ka cube root woh number hai jis ka cube 8 ho, is liye \(x^{3}=8\) likha. Phir 8 ko left side par le aaye taake right side zero ho jaaye; zero ke saath hi hum factorize karke har factor ko alag alag zero rakh sakte hain. Aur 8 ko \(2^{3}\) likha taake difference of cubes ka formula saaf nazar aaye.

Step 2: Difference of cubes se factorize karein
\[a^{3}-b^{3}=(a-b)(a^{2}+ab+b^{2})\]
\[(x-2)(x^{2}+2x+4)=0\]
Kyun: Formula mein \(a=x\) aur \(b=2\) rakha, to \(ab=2x\) aur \(b^{2}=4\) bane. Ab do factors ka product zero hai, aur agar do cheezon ka product zero ho to kam az kam ek factor zaroor zero hota hai. Is liye ab dono factors ko baari baari zero rakhenge.
Dhyan dein: difference of cubes mein doosre bracket ke andar teeno terms plus hote hain, \(x^{2}+2x+4\). Yahan beech wali term par minus laga dena bohat aam ghalti hai.

Step 3: Linear factor se real root
\[x-2=0\]
\[x=2\]
Kyun: Pehla factor zero rakhte hi real cube root foran mil jaata hai. Yeh woh jawab hai jo aap pehle se jaante the: \(2\times2\times2=8\).

Step 4: Quadratic factor ko solve karein
\[x=\dfrac{-2\pm\sqrt{4-16}}{2}\]
\[x=\dfrac{-2\pm\sqrt{-12}}{2}\]
\[x=\dfrac{-2\pm2\sqrt{3}i}{2}\]
\[x=-1\pm\sqrt{3}i\]
Kyun: \(x^{2}+2x+4\) ke real factors nahin bante (discriminant \(4-16\) negative hai), is liye quadratic formula \(x=\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^{2}-4ac}}{2a}\) lagaya, jahan \(a=1,\ b=2,\ c=4\). Negative number ka square root yahan \(i\) le kar aata hai: \(\sqrt{-12}=\sqrt{4}\sqrt{3}\sqrt{-1}=2\sqrt{3}i\). Aakhir mein numerator ke dono terms ko 2 se divide kiya.
Dhyan dein: 2 se sirf pehli term nahin, numerator ki dono terms divide hoti hain.

Step 5: Complex roots ko omega mein likhein
\[-1+\sqrt{3}i=2\cdot\dfrac{-1+\sqrt{3}i}{2}\]
\[-1+\sqrt{3}i=2\omega\]
\[-1-\sqrt{3}i=2\omega^{2}\]
Kyun: Hum ne 2 ko bahar nikaala aur andar 2 se divide kar diya, is se value nahin badli. Ab andar bilkul \(\frac{-1+\sqrt{3}i}{2}\) bacha, jo \(\omega\) hai; isi tarah doosra \(\omega^{2}\) ban gaya. Yeh shakal yaad rakhne mein aasaan hai: 8 ke roots \(2\) ko \(1,\ \omega,\ \omega^{2}\) se multiply karke milte hain.

Tasdeeq: har root ka cube lein
\[(2\omega)^{3}=8\omega^{3}=8\]
\[(2\omega^{2})^{3}=8\omega^{6}=8\]
Kyun: \(\omega^{3}=1\) aur \(\omega^{6}=(\omega^{3})^{2}=1\), is liye dono complex roots ka cube waqai 8 aata hai (aur \(2^{3}=8\) to hai hi). Teeno roots check ho gaye.
blocks.final_answer: \(8\) ke teen cube roots: \(2,\ 2\omega,\ 2\omega^{2}\), yaani \(2,\ -1+\sqrt{3}i,\ -1-\sqrt{3}i\). Matlab: real root sirf ek hai (2), aur baqi do roots aapas mein conjugate (jora: sirf \(i\) wale hisse ka sign ulta) hain.

blocks.prompt: 1 (ii) Find the three cube roots of \(-8\). [The book prints this part as \(8\), the same as part (i); its answer key gives the cube roots of \(-8\). See the book correction below.]
blocks.explanation: Dekhiye, yeh cube root wala sawal hai. Humein number \(-8\) diya gaya hai aur woh tamam numbers \(x\) find karne hain jin ka cube (teesri power) \(-8\) ho. Bohat se students sirf ek real jawab likh kar ruk jaate hain, lekin yaad rakhiye: har non-zero number ke teen cube roots hote hain, ek real aur do complex. Teeno tak pohanchne ka pakka tareeqa yeh hai: pehle \(x^{3}=-8\) ko "kuch = 0" ki shakal mein likhenge, phir sum of cubes ke formula se factorize karenge. Linear factor (jis mein \(x\) ki power 1 ho) se real root milega aur quadratic factor se do complex roots. Aakhir mein complex roots ko \(\omega\) ki madad se saaf shakal mein likh denge. Yahan number negative hai, is liye \(x^{3}+8=0\) banega aur difference ki jagah sum of cubes ka formula lagega.
steps:
Step 1: Sawal ko equation mein badlein
\[x^{3}=-8\]
\[x^{3}+8=0\]
\[x^{3}+2^{3}=0\]
Kyun: \(-8\) ka cube root woh number hai jis ka cube \(-8\) ho. Dono sides mein 8 jama kiya to right side zero ho gayi. Ab left side par do cubes ka sum (jama) hai, \(x^{3}+2^{3}\).

Step 2: Sum of cubes se factorize karein
\[a^{3}+b^{3}=(a+b)(a^{2}-ab+b^{2})\]
\[(x+2)(x^{2}-2x+4)=0\]
Kyun: Formula mein \(a=x\), \(b=2\) rakha. Product zero hai, is liye ek factor zaroor zero hoga.
Dhyan dein: signs ka khayal rakhiye: pehle bracket mein plus, aur doosre bracket mein sirf beech wali term minus (\(-2x\)). Sum aur difference ke formulas ke signs aapas mein mat milaiye.

Step 3: Linear factor se real root
\[x+2=0\]
\[x=-2\]
Kyun: Negative number ka real cube root bhi negative hota hai: \((-2)^{3}=(-2)(-2)(-2)=-8\). (Square root mein aisa nahin hota, lekin cube root mein odd power minus ko qaim rakhti hai.)

Step 4: Quadratic factor ko solve karein
\[x=\dfrac{2\pm\sqrt{4-16}}{2}\]
\[x=\dfrac{2\pm2\sqrt{3}i}{2}\]
\[x=1\pm\sqrt{3}i\]
Kyun: Quadratic formula mein \(a=1,\ b=-2,\ c=4\) hain, is liye \(-b=2\) bana. Andar \(\sqrt{4-16}=\sqrt{-12}=2\sqrt{3}i\), aur phir numerator ki dono terms ko 2 se divide kiya.
Dhyan dein: \(b=-2\) hai, to \(-b\) positive 2 hoga; yahan sign ki ghalti se poora jawab ulta ho jaata hai.

Step 5: Complex roots ko omega mein likhein
\[1-\sqrt{3}i=-2\cdot\dfrac{-1+\sqrt{3}i}{2}\]
\[1-\sqrt{3}i=-2\omega\]
\[1+\sqrt{3}i=-2\omega^{2}\]
Kyun: Is dafa hum ne \(-2\) bahar nikaala. Minus bahar nikaalne se andar ki har term ka sign ulat jaata hai, is liye \(1-\sqrt{3}i\) ke andar \(-1+\sqrt{3}i\) bacha, jo \(2\) se divide ho kar \(\omega\) hai. Isi tarah \(1+\sqrt{3}i=-2\omega^{2}\).

Tasdeeq: har root ka cube lein
\[(-2\omega)^{3}=-8\omega^{3}=-8\]
\[(-2\omega^{2})^{3}=-8\omega^{6}=-8\]
Kyun: Odd power (3) minus sign ko qaim rakhti hai, aur \(\omega^{3}=\omega^{6}=1\). Dono complex roots ka cube \(-8\) aaya, jawab sahih hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(-8\) ke teen cube roots: \(-2,\ -2\omega,\ -2\omega^{2}\), yaani \(-2,\ 1-\sqrt{3}i,\ 1+\sqrt{3}i\). Ghaur kijiye: yeh part (i) ke roots ke bilkul negative hain, kyunke \(-8\) bhi \(8\) ka negative hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab part (ii) mein \(8\) chhaapti hai, jo sirf part (i) ko dohrata hai. Answer key (ii) ka jawab \(\{-2,\ -2\omega,\ -2\omega^{2}\}\) deti hai, aur yeh \(-8\) ke cube roots hain; yaani print mein minus sign reh gaya aur asal number \(-8\) hai. Hum ne \(x^{3}=-8\) solve kiya. (Agar printed \(8\) hi lein to jawab part (i) wala hoga: \(2,\ 2\omega,\ 2\omega^{2}\).)

blocks.prompt: 1 (iii) Find the three cube roots of \(27\).
blocks.explanation: Dekhiye, yeh cube root wala sawal hai. Humein number 27 diya gaya hai aur woh tamam numbers \(x\) find karne hain jin ka cube (teesri power) 27 ho. Bohat se students sirf ek real jawab likh kar ruk jaate hain, lekin yaad rakhiye: har non-zero number ke teen cube roots hote hain, ek real aur do complex. Teeno tak pohanchne ka pakka tareeqa yeh hai: pehle \(x^{3}=27\) ko "kuch = 0" ki shakal mein likhenge, phir difference of cubes ke formula se factorize karenge. Linear factor (jis mein \(x\) ki power 1 ho) se real root milega aur quadratic factor se do complex roots. Aakhir mein complex roots ko \(\omega\) ki madad se saaf shakal mein likh denge. Pehle check kar lijiye ke 27 perfect cube hai: \(3\times3\times3=27\).
steps:
Step 1: Sawal ko equation mein badlein
\[x^{3}=27\]
\[x^{3}-3^{3}=0\]
Kyun: 27 ka cube root woh number hai jis ka cube 27 ho. 27 ko left par la kar right side zero ki, aur \(27=3^{3}\) likha taake difference of cubes ka formula seedha lag sake.

Step 2: Difference of cubes se factorize karein
\[(x-3)(x^{2}+3x+9)=0\]
Kyun: Formula \(a^{3}-b^{3}=(a-b)(a^{2}+ab+b^{2})\) mein \(a=x\), \(b=3\) rakha: \(ab=3x\) aur \(b^{2}=9\). Doosre bracket mein teeno terms plus hain.

Step 3: Real root
\[x-3=0\]
\[x=3\]
Kyun: Product zero ho to koi ek factor zero hota hai; pehla factor zero rakhne se real root 3 mila.

Step 4: Quadratic factor ko solve karein
\[x=\dfrac{-3\pm\sqrt{9-36}}{2}\]
\[x=\dfrac{-3\pm\sqrt{-27}}{2}\]
\[x=\dfrac{-3\pm3\sqrt{3}i}{2}\]
Kyun: Quadratic formula mein \(a=1,\ b=3,\ c=9\); \(b^{2}-4ac=9-36=-27\). Ab \(\sqrt{-27}=\sqrt{9}\sqrt{3}\sqrt{-1}=3\sqrt{3}i\). Yahan 2 se divide karne par fraction hi rehta hai, kyunke 3 aur 2 cancel nahin hote; isi shakal mein chhor dein.
Dhyan dein: \(\sqrt{27}\) ko \(3\sqrt{3}\) likhna na bhooliye; \(27=9\times3\) aur 9 ka square root 3 hai.

Step 5: Complex roots ko omega mein likhein
\[\dfrac{-3+3\sqrt{3}i}{2}=3\omega\]
\[\dfrac{-3-3\sqrt{3}i}{2}=3\omega^{2}\]
Kyun: Numerator mein 3 common hai. Use bahar nikaalein to \(3\cdot\frac{-1\pm\sqrt{3}i}{2}\) bachta hai, aur andar wali cheez bilkul \(\omega\) ya \(\omega^{2}\) hai.

Tasdeeq: har root ka cube lein
\[(3\omega)^{3}=27\omega^{3}=27\]
\[(3\omega^{2})^{3}=27\omega^{6}=27\]
Kyun: \(3^{3}=27\) aur \(\omega^{3}=\omega^{6}=1\). Teeno roots ka cube 27 hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(27\) ke teen cube roots: \(3,\ 3\omega,\ 3\omega^{2}\), yaani \(3,\ \frac{-3+3\sqrt{3}i}{2},\ \frac{-3-3\sqrt{3}i}{2}\). Pattern dekhiye: real root ko \(1,\ \omega,\ \omega^{2}\) se multiply karo, teeno roots mil jaate hain.

blocks.prompt: 1 (iv) Find the three cube roots of \(64\).
blocks.explanation: Dekhiye, yeh cube root wala sawal hai. Humein number 64 diya gaya hai aur woh tamam numbers \(x\) find karne hain jin ka cube (teesri power) 64 ho. Bohat se students sirf ek real jawab likh kar ruk jaate hain, lekin yaad rakhiye: har non-zero number ke teen cube roots hote hain, ek real aur do complex. Teeno tak pohanchne ka pakka tareeqa yeh hai: pehle \(x^{3}=64\) ko "kuch = 0" ki shakal mein likhenge, phir difference of cubes ke formula se factorize karenge. Linear factor (jis mein \(x\) ki power 1 ho) se real root milega aur quadratic factor se do complex roots. Aakhir mein complex roots ko \(\omega\) ki madad se saaf shakal mein likh denge. Yahan \(64=4^{3}\) hai, to real root 4 hoga; asal kaam do complex roots nikaalna hai.
steps:
Step 1: Sawal ko equation mein badlein
\[x^{3}=64\]
\[x^{3}-4^{3}=0\]
Kyun: 64 ka cube root woh number hai jis ka cube 64 ho, aur \(4\times4\times4=64\), is liye \(64=4^{3}\) likha. Right side zero kar di taake factorize kar sakein.
Dhyan dein: \(64=8^{2}\) bhi hai, lekin yahan humein cube chahiye, square nahin; \(8\) cube root nahin hai.

Step 2: Difference of cubes se factorize karein
\[(x-4)(x^{2}+4x+16)=0\]
Kyun: \(a=x\), \(b=4\) rakhne par \(ab=4x\) aur \(b^{2}=16\) bante hain, aur formula \((a-b)(a^{2}+ab+b^{2})\) se yeh factors mil gaye.

Step 3: Real root
\[x-4=0\]
\[x=4\]
Kyun: Pehla factor zero rakha; zero product ka matlab hai ke koi ek factor zero hai.

Step 4: Quadratic factor ko solve karein
\[x=\dfrac{-4\pm\sqrt{16-64}}{2}\]
\[x=\dfrac{-4\pm\sqrt{-48}}{2}\]
\[x=\dfrac{-4\pm4\sqrt{3}i}{2}\]
\[x=-2\pm2\sqrt{3}i\]
Kyun: Quadratic formula mein \(a=1,\ b=4,\ c=16\); \(b^{2}-4ac=16-64=-48\). Ab \(48=16\times3\), is liye \(\sqrt{-48}=\sqrt{16}\sqrt{3}\,i=4\sqrt{3}i\). Aakhir mein \(-4\) aur \(4\sqrt{3}i\) dono ko 2 se divide kiya.

Step 5: Complex roots ko omega mein likhein
\[-2+2\sqrt{3}i=4\cdot\dfrac{-1+\sqrt{3}i}{2}\]
\[-2+2\sqrt{3}i=4\omega\]
\[-2-2\sqrt{3}i=4\omega^{2}\]
Kyun: Ulti taraf se check kijiye: \(4\times\frac{-1}{2}=-2\) aur \(4\times\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=2\sqrt{3}\). Yaani 4 bahar nikaalne se andar \(\omega\) (ya \(\omega^{2}\)) bach jaata hai.

Tasdeeq: har root ka cube lein
\[(4\omega)^{3}=64\omega^{3}=64\]
\[(4\omega^{2})^{3}=64\omega^{6}=64\]
Kyun: \(4^{3}=64\) aur \(\omega^{3}=\omega^{6}=1\). Teeno roots sahih hain.
blocks.final_answer: \(64\) ke teen cube roots: \(4,\ 4\omega,\ 4\omega^{2}\), yaani \(4,\ -2+2\sqrt{3}i,\ -2-2\sqrt{3}i\). (Answer key yahan ghalat jawab deti hai; neeche "Kitab ki ghalti" dekhiye.)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Part (iv) ke liye answer key \(\{-3,\ -3\omega,\ -3\omega^{2}\}\) chhaapti hai. Yeh \(-27\) ke cube roots hain (kyunke \((-3)^{3}=-27\)), printed \(64\) ke nahin; key ki list asal mein \(8,\ -8,\ 27,\ -27,\ 64\) ke hisaab se hai, printed numbers ke hisaab se nahin. \(64\) ke sahih cube roots \(4,\ 4\omega,\ 4\omega^{2}\) hain.

blocks.prompt: 1 (v) Find the three cube roots of \(-625\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh bhi cube root ka sawal hai, lekin ab ek nayi mushkil hai: \(-625\) perfect cube nahin hai (koi whole number aisa nahin jis ka cube 625 ho). Is liye pichle parts ki tarah whole numbers se factorize karna mushkil ho jaata hai. Behtar tareeqa yeh hai: pehle sirf ek real cube root dhoondein, aur us ke liye 625 mein se perfect cube alag karein (\(625=125\times5\)). Phir woh qaida (rule) lagayein jo pichle chaar parts mein baar baar nazar aaya: agar ek cube root \(k\) ho to teeno cube roots \(k,\ k\omega,\ k\omega^{2}\) hain. Pehle step mein hum yeh qaida saabit bhi karenge taake aap ise aankh band karke nahin, samajh kar use karein.
steps:
Step 1: k, k omega, k omega squared teeno cube roots kyun hain
\[(k\omega)^{3}=k^{3}\omega^{3}=k^{3}\]
\[(k\omega^{2})^{3}=k^{3}\omega^{6}=k^{3}\]
Kyun: \(\omega^{3}=1\) hai, is liye kisi cube root ko \(\omega\) ya \(\omega^{2}\) se multiply karne se us ka cube nahin badalta. Yeh teeno numbers aapas mein mukhtalif (different) hain, aur cubic equation (teesri degree ki equation) ke zyada se zyada teen roots hote hain, is liye yahi teeno poore cube roots hain, koi aur nahin.

Step 2: Real cube root dhoondein
\[625=125\times5\]
\[\sqrt[3]{-625}=\sqrt[3]{-125}\cdot\sqrt[3]{5}\]
\[\sqrt[3]{-625}=-5\sqrt[3]{5}\]
Kyun: 625 ko aise todha ke ek hissa perfect cube ho: \(-125=(-5)^{3}\). Product ka cube root, cube roots ka product hota hai, is liye \(\sqrt[3]{-125}=-5\) bahar aa gaya aur \(\sqrt[3]{5}\) andar reh gaya. Bilkul waise hi jaise \(\sqrt{12}=2\sqrt{3}\) karte hain, bas yahan square ki jagah cube hai.
Dhyan dein: \(625=25\times25\) se kuch nahin banta, kyunke 25 perfect cube nahin; perfect cube factor 125 hai.

Step 3: Baqi do cube roots
\[k=-5\sqrt[3]{5}\]
\[k\omega=-5\sqrt[3]{5}\,\omega\]
\[k\omega^{2}=-5\sqrt[3]{5}\,\omega^{2}\]
Kyun: Step 1 ka qaida \(k=-5\sqrt[3]{5}\) ke saath lagaya. Real root ko \(\omega\) aur \(\omega^{2}\) se multiply karte hi baqi do roots mil gaye; koi lamba quadratic formula nahin lagana para.

Step 4: Yahi roots a + ib ki shakal mein
\[-\omega=\dfrac{1-\sqrt{3}i}{2}\]
\[k\omega=\dfrac{5\sqrt[3]{5}}{2}(1-\sqrt{3}i)\]
\[k\omega^{2}=\dfrac{5\sqrt[3]{5}}{2}(1+\sqrt{3}i)\]
Kyun: \(k\omega=5\sqrt[3]{5}\cdot(-\omega)\) likh sakte hain, aur \(-\omega\), \(-\omega^{2}\) ki values \(\frac{1\mp\sqrt{3}i}{2}\) hain (minus bahar se andar jaane par har sign ulat jaata hai). Andaaza lagane ke liye: roots taqreeban \(-8.55\) aur \(4.27\mp7.40i\) hain.

Tasdeeq: real root ka cube lein
\[(-5\sqrt[3]{5})^{3}=(-5)^{3}(\sqrt[3]{5})^{3}\]
\[=-125\times5=-625\]
Kyun: Cube root ki definition hi yeh hai ke \(\sqrt[3]{5}\) ka cube 5 ho. Baqi do roots ka cube Step 1 ki wajah se khud ba khud \(-625\) hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(-625\) ke teen cube roots: \(-5\sqrt[3]{5},\ -5\sqrt[3]{5}\,\omega,\ -5\sqrt[3]{5}\,\omega^{2}\). Matlab: ek real root (taqreeban \(-8.55\)) aur us ko \(\omega\), \(\omega^{2}\) se multiply karke do complex roots.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Part (v) ke liye answer key \(\{4,\ 4\omega,\ 4\omega^{2}\}\) chhaapti hai. Yeh \(64\) (part (iv)) ke cube roots hain, printed \(-625\) ke nahin; key mein \(-625\) ka jawab hai hi nahin. \(-625\) ke sahih cube roots \(-5\sqrt[3]{5},\ -5\sqrt[3]{5}\,\omega,\ -5\sqrt[3]{5}\,\omega^{2}\) hain.
